title: Design a real-time chat system
prompt: Build the backend for a WhatsApp-style messaging app: millions of users hold persistent connections and expect messages delivered in well under a second, even when the recipient is offline. The dominant forcing constraint is fan-out delivery under massive connection load — a single message may need to reach many recipients across many servers, and history must survive forever. Draw how a message travels from sender to recipient(s): show the connection/gateway tier that terminates persistent connections, a stateless chat service, an asynchronous delivery path for fan-out and offline users, durable storage for message history, and a cache for presence and recent messages. Wire the service to each of these so several reasonable topologies pass — but a bare client-to-database sketch fails.

criteria.label: Clients originate messages
criteria.metWhy: Good — the flow starts from real users sending and receiving messages.
criteria.why: Add a User/Client node — chat begins with people sending messages from their devices.

criteria.label: A gateway/connection tier terminates persistent connections
criteria.metWhy: Solid — a gateway tier fronts the persistent (WebSocket) connections from millions of clients.
criteria.why: Millions of clients hold long-lived connections. Add a Load Balancer or API Gateway as the connection tier that terminates them before reaching the service.

criteria.label: A stateless chat service processes messages
criteria.metWhy: Good — a dedicated service handles routing, delivery, and persistence of messages.
criteria.why: Add a Server/Service tier to handle message routing and delivery logic, kept stateless so it can scale horizontally behind the gateway.

criteria.label: An async queue handles fan-out and offline delivery
criteria.metWhy: Excellent — a queue decouples delivery so fan-out and offline recipients are handled asynchronously.
criteria.why: Fan-out to many recipients (and offline users) shouldn't block the sender. Add a Queue to drive asynchronous message delivery.

criteria.label: Messages are persisted in durable storage
criteria.metWhy: Good — message history is durably stored so it survives restarts and offline gaps.
criteria.why: Chat history must persist forever. Add a Database as the durable source of truth for messages.

criteria.label: Presence / recent messages served from a cache
criteria.metWhy: Nice — a cache absorbs presence lookups and hot recent-message reads.
criteria.why: Presence (who's online) and recent messages are read constantly. Add a Cache so these hot reads don't hammer the database.

criteria.label: Service drives delivery through the queue
criteria.metWhy: Good — the service publishes to the queue so fan-out is decoupled from the request path.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Queue so message delivery and fan-out run asynchronously.

criteria.label: Service persists messages to the database
criteria.metWhy: Good — the service writes message history to durable storage.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Database so every message is durably stored and retrievable.

criteria.label: Service reads presence/recent state from the cache
criteria.metWhy: Good — the service checks presence and recent messages via the cache.
criteria.why: Connect the Service to the Cache so presence and recent-message lookups stay fast under load.
